acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

data.reason: Diane, the CFO, froze all new vendor projects after a missed Q3. Nobody showed her what the homegrown system cost. Renee blames timing, but Owen's payback number was never built.

trigger.action: Lead with price changes in minutes, not a quarter of work.
trigger.why: Owen, VP of Product, reached out because every pricing change on their homegrown system took a quarter.
trigger.quote: every pricing change takes them a quarter

decider.action: Give finance a reason billing is urgent, not a nice to have.
decider.why: Renee never spoke to Diane, the CFO. Owen said finance saw the project as a nice to have.
decider.quote: if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded.

competitor.action: Answer the fear of switching: no card re-entry, moving in stages.
competitor.why: Against doing nothing, Owen asked about keeping landlords' cards and moving in stages. His engineering lead feared renewal season.
competitor.quote: we don't touch billing before renewal season.

message.action: Cut 'grow revenue' for billing and lead with the price-change demo.
message.why: Owen rejected Renee's revenue pitch, but the demo of changing a price in a few clicks excited him.
message.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing

proof.action: Add a payback story from a company that replaced homegrown billing.
proof.why: Owen got the general ROI deck but needed his own number for Diane, and someone who had done it.
proof.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.

words.action: Describe homegrown billing as 'a tax on the roadmap'.
words.why: Owen used this phrase for his own problem, and it frames the cost in product time, not revenue.
